nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Project instructions mandate querying the pre-built knowledge graph at graphify-out/ before raw grep or source browsing, because a scoped subgraph is usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, reducing context cost.

nodes.label: graphify query command
nodes.rationale: First-choice tool for codebase questions when graphify-out/graph.json exists; returns a scoped subgraph instead of whole-file dumps.

nodes.label: graphify update (AST-only refresh)
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code to keep the graph current; chosen because it is AST-only and therefore incurs no API cost.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md architecture review doc
nodes.rationale: Reserved for broad architecture review only, since it is large; query/path/explain are preferred first.

nodes.label: GiggleGarden YouTube Automation System
nodes.rationale: A three-project Windows/.NET 8 pipeline (VideoGen, TokenCapture, Uploader) that produces and publishes multilingual kids' content on a daily Task Scheduler cadence.

nodes.label: VideoGen project
nodes.rationale: Generates finished videos via script -> TTS -> images -> FFmpeg. Each run emits BOTH a 1920x1080 landscape video and a 1080x1920 Short so one generation pass covers both YouTube surfaces.

nodes.label: TokenCapture project
nodes.rationale: Run once interactively with a browser consent flow as the channel-owner account, so that the unattended daily Uploader never needs interactive sign-in; it persists a refresh token to a token store path.

nodes.label: Uploader project
nodes.rationale: Runs daily via Windows Task Scheduler, scans D:\Business\Videos for .mp4 files, generates or reads a sidecar JSON, and uploads only approved items. Published to D:\Business\UploaderApp for the scheduled task.

nodes.label: Human Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated metadata always lands with approved:false and nothing uploads until flipped to true. Deliberately kept as a 10-second human glance because the audience is children and generated visuals need human eyes every time. If the operator writes their own sidecar JSON with approved:true up front, the trend+Claude metadata step is skipped entirely.

nodes.label: Sidecar JSON metadata format
nodes.rationale: A per-video JSON file (title, description, tags, approved) written next to the .mp4. Acts as the shared contract between VideoGen output and Uploader input, and as the carrier of the approval flag.

nodes.label: YouTube API Quota Budget
nodes.rationale: Each upload costs ~1,600 units and each trend search ~100 units against a 10,000/day cap; MaxUploadsPerRun is set to 3 to stay comfortably under the cap.

nodes.label: Private-first rollout policy
nodes.rationale: PrivacyStatus is kept at "private" until an end-to-end test passes and YouTube Studio shows correct metadata plus the made-for-kids flag; only then is it flipped to "public". Limits blast radius of a misconfigured automated upload.

nodes.label: Uploader appsettings.json configuration
nodes.rationale: Holds TokenStorePath (must match where TokenCapture saved the token), the Anthropic API key for auto-generated metadata, PrivacyStatus and MaxUploadsPerRun. Credentials are stored outside the repo (a C:\Secure path) rather than checked in.

nodes.label: Daily Task Scheduler two-job flow
nodes.rationale: Job 1 (~6am) runs VideoGen for one video with a rotating language; the operator approves; job 2 (~4pm) runs Uploader. Upload time targets the kids'-content viewing peak of roughly 3-7pm local, and the task is set to run whether the user is logged on or not and to wake the computer.

nodes.label: Multilingual content strategy (en/hi/pa)
nodes.rationale: Videos rotate across English, Hindi and Punjabi; descriptions carry an English, Hindi and Punjabi paragraph and tags include Devanagari terms. NirmalaB.ttf is chosen as the font because it ships with Windows and covers both Devanagari and Gurmukhi, avoiding a font-licensing/bundling step.

nodes.label: Azure Speech TTS narration
nodes.rationale: Free F0 tier (0.5M chars/month) is deemed sufficient to start; cost only becomes material later at roughly $0.05/video.

nodes.label: OpenAI scene illustration generation
nodes.rationale: Seven scenes at medium quality is the dominant cost driver at roughly $0.30 per video.

nodes.label: Claude script writing and topic selection
nodes.rationale: Claude writes the script (~$0.02/video) and can also pick the topic when --topic is omitted; it is additionally used with trend search to auto-generate upload metadata.
nodes.norm_label: claude script writing and topic selection

nodes.label: Per-video cost model (< $0.50)
nodes.rationale: Script ~$0.02 + TTS ~$0.05 + images ~$0.30 keeps total well under $0.50 per video, which is the economic premise that makes daily unattended generation viable.

nodes.label: D:\Business\Videos shared output directory
nodes.rationale: Filesystem drop folder acting as the handoff queue between VideoGen and Uploader; no database or message broker is used.

nodes.label: GiggleGarden automation setup guide (project copy)
nodes.rationale: Duplicate of the root README kept inside the gigglegarden-automation solution folder so the setup instructions travel with the source tree.

nodes.label: TokenCapture Debug build output manifest
nodes.rationale: MSBuild-generated list confirming TokenCapture ships Google.Apis, Google.Apis.Auth, Google.Apis.Core and Google.Apis.YouTube.v3 — i.e. it links the YouTube Data API client purely to run the OAuth consent flow.

nodes.label: Uploader Debug build output manifest
nodes.rationale: Shows Uploader adds the Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration stack (Json, Binder, FileExtensions, FileProviders) on top of the Google.Apis set, matching its appsettings.json-driven configuration.

nodes.label: Uploader publish manifest to D:\Business\UploaderApp
nodes.rationale: Confirms the documented publish target: dotnet publish -c Release -o D:\Business\UploaderApp, the exact path Task Scheduler launches Uploader.exe from. appsettings.json is published alongside the exe, so the deployed copy carries its own configuration.

nodes.label: Google.Apis.YouTube.v3 client dependency
nodes.rationale: Shared by both TokenCapture and Uploader; it is the concrete mechanism behind the refresh-token handoff and the quota accounting described in the README.

nodes.label: Gigi Colors (EN) video transcript
nodes.rationale: Short English colors-lesson transcript following the intro/lesson/outro shape of generated kids' content; the character name is transcribed as 'TG' which is likely an ASR mishearing of the Gigi/GiggleGarden mascot.

nodes.label: Gigi the little duckling (channel mascot)
nodes.rationale: Recurring duckling character; the README's example title 'Five Little Ducks | Fun Counting Song for Kids' suggests ducks are a deliberate recurring motif for the GiggleGarden brand.
